turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale, I have a client call at 4:40, so let's keep this short. Owen found out his English mark on his phone, in the middle of class. Why was I not phoned before that zero was entered?
I don't think this is productive.
Then answer the question and we'll both be done sooner. Who entered the zero, and when did you first try to call me?
I'm going to go. I have a class in ten minutes.

You can go to your class once you've answered me. That zero is in the gradebook right now, and if you walk out without saying who entered it and when you first tried to reach me, I'm going straight to the principal's office.
Email the principal if you want. I'm done here.
Then I'll be in the principal's office today, asking why my son's zero went into the gradebook before anyone called his mother. Sit down, Hale, and tell me who entered it and when.
